g.text: Though KC is part of Apache Kafka download, but for using it, we need to start

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: KC daemons on servers. It is important to understand that KC cluster is

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: different from Kafka message broker cluster, KC has its own dedicated cluster

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: where on each machine, KC daemons are running (java processes called as

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: A KC worker instance is started on each server with a Kafka broker address,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: topics for internal use and group id. Each worker instance is stateless and does

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: not share info with other workers. But they coordinate with each other,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: belonging to same group id, via the internal kafka topics. This is similar to how

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Kafka consumer group works and is implemented underneath in a similar way.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Each worker instantiates a Connector (Source or Sink Connector) which defines

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: configurations of the associated Task(Source or Sink Task). A Task is actually

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: a runnable thread which does the actual work of transferring data and

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: committing the offsets. e.g. S3SinkTask is a runnable thread which takes care of

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: transferring data from Kafka of a single topic-partition to S3.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Worker instantiates pool of Task threads,based on info provided by Connector.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Before creating task threads, Workers decide among themselves which part of

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: data each of them is going to process, through internal Kafka topics.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: It is important to note here, that there is no central server in KC cluster and KC

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: is not responsible for launching worker instances, or restarting them on failure.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: If a worker process dies, the cluster is rebalanced to distribute the work fairly

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: over the remaining workers. If a new worker is started, a rebalance ensures it

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: takes over some work from the existing workers. This rebalancing is an existing

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: KC exposes REST api to create, modify and destroy connectors.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: A Source Connector (with help of Source Tasks) is responsible for getting data

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: into kafka while a Sink Connector (with help of Sink Tasks) is responsible for

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Internally, what happens is, at regular intervals, data is polled by source task

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: from data source and written to kafka and then offsets are committed. Similarly

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: on the sink side, data is pushed at regular intervals by Sink tasks from Kafka to

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: destination system and offsets are committed. For example, I looked into the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: code of S3sink connector and found that, a sink task keeps putting data for a

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: specific kafka topic-partition to bytebuffer and then at a configurable time (by

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: default 30 seconds), the data is accumulated and written to S3 files. Also, it

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: uses a deterministic partitioner which ensures that in case of failures, even if

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: the same data is written twice, the operation is idempotent. Deterministic

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: partitioner means that a for a given same set of records, there will be same

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: number of files with each file having exactly same data. As such, it ensures

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
